content:
Transformers use attention instead of recurrence mainly because attention lets the model directly access and weigh all parts of the input sequence simultaneously, rather than processing it step-by-step like recurrence does. This means the model can capture long-range dependencies more efficiently and in parallel, avoiding the slow, sequential bottleneck of recurrent networks.

Think of recurrence as reading a sentence word by word, remembering everything in a hidden state that updates each step. Attention, by contrast, is like having the whole sentence visible at once and focusing on the most relevant words directly, no matter where they are.

The key takeaway: attention enables parallel, global context access, making training faster and capturing relationships across distant positions more effectively than recurrence.
